text: With Owen's sign-off on a change ticket, Mara edits the rule's configured source from 198.51.0.0/16 to the vendor's actual 198.51.100.16/28. No new rule, no new port -- just a scope correction.
Even a one-line edit goes through a change ticket, because this exact rule caused the incident and deserves a second set of eyes before going live.
Test 1: a connection from the vendor's real address inside the new range comes back Allow. The legitimate support path still works.
Test 2: a connection from an address that was inside the old broad range but outside the vendor's real /28 comes back Deny. That's the result that actually proves the gap is closed.
A fix tested only one way is half-validated. Confirming production isn't broken, and confirming the exposure is gone, are two separate proofs.
